T: Mind your vowels and pass the cucumber sandwiches.
D: A cockney flower seller takes lessons from an arrogant professor of phonetics who bets he can pass her off as a lady.
P: Serve the Scotch eggs when Alfred Doolittle turns up at Wimpole Street to see what his daughter is worth to the professor.
S: paper-thin slices on soft white bread with butter, cream cheese and dill, Eliza's first outing
The Edwardian race day tea sandwich done properly: paper-thin cucumber on soft white bread with whipped butter, cream cheese and dill, crusts off, cut in neat fingers.
soft-boiled, wrapped in sage sausage meat, crumbed, fried, piccalilli, with a little bit of luck
The proper London pub snack: soft-boiled eggs wrapped in sage and pork sausage meat, crumbed and fried, halved warm with piccalilli.
M: seared fillet in mustard, wrapped in mushroom duxelles and puff pastry, sliced for Eliza's big night
The grand English dinner centrepiece: seared beef fillet in mustard, wrapped in mushroom duxelles and puff pastry, baked golden and sliced at the table.
Roasted golden with saffron and garlic. By George, she's got it
Potatoes tossed in saffron butter and garlic, roasted until crisp and golden at the edges.
W: For the bunches of violets Eliza sells under the portico at Covent Garden
A classic English tea table sponge sandwiched with blackberry jam and vanilla cream, finished with pale violet icing and edible flowers.
K: A long cold drink for Pickering in the Wimpole Street study
An English garden long drink: dry gin, elderflower and lemon shaken and lengthened with soda over ice, with cucumber ribbons and mint.

dishes.make_ahead: Make up to 2 hours ahead, covered with a damp tea towel in the fridge so the bread stays soft

steps.text: Toss the cucumber with the salt and drain on paper towel.
Beat the butter with the cream cheese, dill and white pepper.
Spread the bread to the edges, lay cucumber over 8 slices and close with the rest.
Press down gently, cut off the crusts and cut each into 3 fingers.

dishes.make_ahead: Make and crumb the Scotch eggs up to 1 day ahead and keep in the fridge; fry on the night or serve cold

steps.text: Lower 4 eggs into boiling water for 6 1/2 minutes, then into iced water. Peel.
Mix the sausage meat with the sage, mustard, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Flatten a quarter of the mixture on wet hands, wrap it round an egg and seal. Chill 20 minutes.
Roll each in flour, then the beaten eggs, then the panko.
Deep-fry at 170C for 7 minutes until deep golden and cooked through. Drain, halve and serve with piccalilli.

veg.make_ahead: Make and crumb the Scotch eggs up to 1 day ahead and keep in the fridge; fry on the night or serve cold

steps.text: Lower 4 eggs into boiling water for 6 1/2 minutes, then into iced water. Peel.
Squeeze the vegetarian sausages out of their skins and mix with the sage, mustard, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Flatten a quarter of the mixture on wet hands, wrap it round an egg and seal. Chill 20 minutes.
Roll each in flour, then the beaten eggs, then the panko.
Deep-fry at 170C for 6 minutes until deep golden and hot through. Drain, halve and serve with piccalilli.

dishes.make_ahead: Sear the beef and make the duxelles up to 1 day ahead, or wrap it up to 1 day ahead and keep it in the fridge; bake on the night

steps.text: Season the beef with half the salt and pepper, sear all over in the vegetable oil in a very hot pan, brush with the mustard and cool.
Blitz the mushrooms finely and cook with the shallots, garlic, thyme and butter until dry and dark. Cool.
Lay the pastry sheets slightly overlapping, press to join, spread with the mushrooms, sit the beef on top, roll up and seal. Brush with egg and chill 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200C. Toss the potatoes with the olive oil and the rest of the salt and pepper and roast.
Score the pastry and bake the Wellington for medium rare.
Steam the beans for 4 minutes and rest the Wellington 10 minutes before slicing thickly.

veg.n: Embassy Ball mushroom and chestnut Wellington
veg.make_ahead: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead, or wrap the Wellington up to 1 day ahead and keep it in the fridge; bake on the night

steps.text: Blitz the mushrooms finely and cook with the shallots, garlic, thyme and butter until dry and dark, then stir in the chestnuts, spinach and half the salt and pepper. Cool.
Lay the pastry sheets slightly overlapping, press to join, spread the centre with mustard and pile the mushroom filling down the middle in a log. Roll up, seal, brush with egg and chill 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200C. Toss the potatoes with the oil and the rest of the salt and pepper and roast.
Score the pastry and bake the Wellington until deep golden and crisp underneath.
Steam the beans for 4 minutes and rest the Wellington 10 minutes before slicing thickly.

dishes.make_ahead: Par-boil the potatoes up to 1 day ahead; roast on the night

steps.text: Soak the saffron in 2 tbsp hot water.
Boil the potatoes for 8 minutes and drain well.
Melt the butter with the oil, garlic and saffron water, toss through the potatoes and roast at 220C until golden.
Scatter with chopped parsley and salt.

dishes.make_ahead: Bake the sponges up to 1 day ahead and keep them airtight; fill and ice on the day

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C and line two 20cm tins. Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour, vanilla and milk, split between the tins and bake.
Cool the sponges completely.
Whip the cream with 1 tbsp of the icing sugar. Spread one sponge with jam, then cream, and top with the second.
Mix the rest of the icing sugar with lemon juice and the food colouring, spread over the top and finish with the flowers.

dishes.make_ahead: Ribbon the cucumber and squeeze the lemons up to 4 hours ahead and keep cold; shake to order

steps.text: Fill 4 tall glasses with ice and add a couple of cucumber ribbons to each.
Shake the gin, elderflower cordial and lemon juice with ice and strain into the glasses.
Top with soda water and add a mint sprig.

s.note: Thin cucumber with whipped butter, cream cheese, dill and white pepper on soft white bread, crusts off, in fingers
s.how: Slice 2 telegraph cucumbers as thin as you can, toss with 1/2 tsp salt and drain on paper towel for 15 minutes. Beat 100g softened butter with 125g cream cheese, chopped dill and white pepper. Spread 16 slices of soft white bread to the edges, lay cucumber over 8 slices and close with the rest. Press down gently, cut off the crusts and cut each into 3 fingers.

s.note: Jammy eggs in sage and nutmeg pork sausage meat, crumbed and fried golden, with piccalilli
s.how: Lower 4 eggs into boiling water for 6 1/2 minutes, then into iced water, and peel. Mix 400g pork sausage meat with 1 tbsp chopped sage, 1 tsp English mustard, nutmeg, salt and pepper. Flatten a quarter on wet hands, wrap round an egg and seal, then chill 20 minutes. Roll in flour, then 2 beaten eggs, then panko. Deep-fry at 170C for 7 minutes until deep golden and cooked through. Drain, halve and serve with piccalilli.

m.note: Seared beef fillet in mustard and mushroom duxelles wrapped in puff pastry, with roast baby potatoes and green beans
m.how: Season a 1kg centre-cut beef fillet and sear all over in a very hot pan, then brush with 2 tbsp dijon and cool. Blitz 500g mushrooms and cook with 2 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, thyme and 40g butter until dry and dark, then cool. Lay 2 sheets of puff pastry slightly overlapping, spread with the mushrooms, sit the beef on top, roll up and seal, brush with egg and chill 20 minutes. Heat the oven to 200C. Score the pastry and bake 35 to 40 minutes for medium rare, roasting 750g baby potatoes alongside with oil, salt and pepper. Rest the Wellington 10 minutes, steam 300g green beans and slice thickly at the table.

w.note: Butter sponge layered with blackberry jam and vanilla cream, under a pale violet lemon icing with edible flowers
w.how: Heat the oven to 180C and line two 20cm tins. Beat 200g softened butter with 200g caster sugar until pale, beat in 4 eggs one at a time, then fold in 200g self-raising flour, 1 tsp vanilla and 2 tbsp milk. Split between the tins and bake 22 minutes. Cool. Whip 200ml thickened cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar. Spread one sponge with 150g blackberry jam, then the cream, and top with the second sponge. Mix 150g icing sugar with lemon juice and a drop of purple food colouring to a thick icing, spread over the top and finish with edible violets or viola flowers.

d.note: Dry gin, elderflower cordial and lemon over ice, topped with soda, with cucumber ribbons and mint
d.how: Fill 4 tall glasses with ice and add a couple of long cucumber ribbons to each. Shake 180ml gin, 80ml elderflower cordial and the juice of 2 lemons with ice, strain into the glasses, top with soda water and add a mint sprig.
